ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the angle bisector, and $AE$ is the height. Given that $\angle B=50^\circ$ and $\angle C=60^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle EAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \]
\[ \because \angle BAC = 180^\circ - \angle B - \angle C, \]
\[ \therefore \angle BAC = 180^\circ - 50^\circ - 60^\circ = 70^\circ; \]
\[ \because \text{AD is the bisector of the angle}, \]
\[ \therefore \angle DAC = \frac{1}{2} \angle BAC = 35^\circ; \]
\[ \because \text{AE is the altitude}, \]
\[ \therefore \angle AEC = 90^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \angle EAC = 90^\circ - \angle C = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \angle EAD = \angle DAC - \angle EAC = 35^\circ - 30^\circ = \boxed{5^\circ}. \]

Then reason: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°, so ∠BAC=180°−50°−60°=70°. Because AD bisects ∠BAC, ∠DAC=70°÷2=35°. Also because AE is the altitude, AE⊥BC, so in right triangle AEC, ∠AEC=90°, therefore ∠EAC=90°−∠C=90°−60°=30°. ∠EAD is the difference between ∠DAC and ∠EAC, so ∠EAD=35°−30°=5°.
